newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Loral Jan 97 call trades 20,000.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Loral Jan 97 call trades 20,000.

text.p: A big trade in options on shares of Loral Space & Communications Ltd highlighted individual equity options business on Wednesday, traders said.
By 1500 CDT/2000 GMT, 20,134 of the Loral January 1997 15 calls traded, making it by far the most active individual equity option around.
The next most active option was Motorola Inc's October 50 put, with 7,411 contracts changing hands.
John Streibich, a market maker on the floor of the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), where Loral options trade, said Morgan Stanley had sold 20,000 of the January 1997 15 calls.
The brokerage firm sold the options at 3/4 and Streibich said it was opening a position.
He said the trading crowd bought the options.
The trade was effected in four blocks of 5,000 each. The option had open interest of 1,700 contracts through Tuesday.
Loral shares were down 1/2 at 13-1/8 in late trade and did not react to options trade. The stock reached a session high of 13-1/2 and a session low of 12-7/8.
Streibich said traders guessed Morgan Stanley was writing the calls against stock it already owns, a common strategy known as covered call writing.
On the American Stock Exchange (Amex), several Motorola options were active amid volatile trading in the stock after the company warned of a drop in third quarter profits.
By late trade, Motorola was down 1-1/2 at 49-1/8. It reached 46-3/4 in early trading. Volume was heavy at more than 10.35 million shares.
The Motorola October 50 put was most active, followed by the September 50 put and the October 50 call.
Also on the Amex, a spread between the Philip Morris Cos Inc January 1997 50 and 60 call was seen.
The January 1997 50 call, with an open interest through Tuesday of 1,600, traded 5,550 contracts. It was up 3/4 at 41-1/2.
The January 1997 60 call traded 3,500 contracts. It was up 1/4 at 31-1/4 and had open interest of 5,300.
A couple of options on shares of modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp were active as the stock rallied sharply. U.S. Robotics gained 4-3/8 points to 56-7/8 on heavy volume of more than six million shares.
The U.S. Robotics September 55 call, up 1-5/8 at three, traded nearly 1,700 contracts and the October 45 put, down 3/4 at one, traded about 1,850.

Traders said the stock, which was hit last week on talk that some modem manufacturers were experiencing a decline in demand, rallied sharply on rumors it had a new generation high-speed modem in the works.
